summary: Prescott NF lookout on Mingus Mountain: 60-ft steel tower built 1935 to replace a 41-ft wooden one; NRHP-listed 1988; listed standing, current access unconfirmed.

facts.design: 60-ft Pacific Coast Steel tower (1935) with a 7x7 cab; the register says the cab is metal, Wikipedia says wooden

events.note: Mingus Mountain first used as a daily patrol lookout
June 18, 1921 newspaper notice: timber cut for a Forest Service tower that would be 44 feet high
February 1, 1924 notice: one lookout tower on Mingus under construction; the notice does not give its height
May 20, 1927 item: a new lookout took over the tower; summer lookout kept every day and Sunday
1932 account of Forest Lookout William Anderson: tower about forty feet above the ground; lookouts told to leave towers in electrical storms
60-foot Pacific Coast Steel tower built to replace a 41-foot wooden tower
June 1956 fire from a University of Arizona range experiment just outside the forest; came within 300 yards of a lookout station; 13,500 acres burned
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places on January 28, 1988, in a batch with 41 other fire lookout towers
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on August 5, 2003

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the 7x7 cab is metal; Wikipedia says it is wooden with a front porch. The record gives both and does not choose.

resolved_conflicts.field: height of the tower replaced in 1935
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Wikipedia say the replaced tower was 41 feet; a June 1921 newspaper notice planned a 44-foot tower. These may be different structures, and the record does not choose.

corrections.why: 213.4 m (about 700 ft) is far too tall; the register and Wikipedia give a 60-foot tower, about 18 m

notes_for_editor: Brief height 213.4 m is wrong; the tower is 60 ft (about 18.3 m). Current access, staffing and rental status could not be found. Agency is left out of facts: the pages read confirm Prescott National Forest but not the current administering unit. The NRHP nomination PDF (S3) returned 403, the NPGallery asset pages carry no readable text, the Living New Deal page returned 403, and the Facebook pages were unreadable. A 1944 'Twenty years ago' column on Forest Lookouts repeats a 1924 notice and is not counted as a separate event. Page reads for this tower went over the per-tower cap because of failed nomination fetches. Used two web searches.
